theorems.name: K4 frame double cover is Q3
theorems.statement: The eight pairs (slice, central half-turn sheet), with an edge whenever the slice changes and the sheet toggles, are canonically the eight vertices and twelve edges of the cube graph.

theorems.name: Odd face loops reach the deck partner
theorems.statement: Every lifted three-edge K4 face path ends at the opposite frame sheet; in the cube code this is the antipodal vertex.

theorems.name: Tetrahedral transport shortcut relations
theorems.statement: The source half-turn squares to identity, shortest transport intertwines endpoint half-turns, and every two-edge path through a third vertex equals the direct edge followed by the source half-turn.

theorems.name: Endpoint-parity path transport theorem
theorems.statement: For any K4 path of m edges, transport equals T_start,end H_start^(m-1) when endpoints differ and H_start^m when the path is closed. Consequently closed even paths are identity and closed odd paths are the Euler tangent half-turn.

theorems.name: Flat development on the cube frame cover
theorems.statement: Two K4 paths with the same base endpoint and length parity have identical shortest-connection transport; after lifting endpoints to Q3, transport is path independent and the deck involution acts by the local tangent half-turn.

theorems.name: Unique nonzero S4-fixed central curvature class
theorems.statement: The all-edge-one cochain evaluates to one on every K4 triangle and represents the unique nonzero class fixed by the full S4 action in C1(K4;F2)/delta C0(K4;F2).
theorems.boundary: This central phase class is typed separately from the O(2) chirality-reversal handoff class.

theorems.name: Spin order-four refinement
theorems.statement: The vector face holonomy has order two while its normalized Spin lift has order four; reversing face orientation changes only the Spin sign.

theorems.name: Cube/BCC return count
theorems.statement: For the eight sign steps (+/-1,+/-1,+/-1), the number of 2n-step returns is choose(2n,n)^3 and the return probability is ((1/2)_n/n!)^3.

theorems.name: Euler-Ramanujan finite-cover bridge
theorems.statement: The same eight-state cube realizes the central frame double cover resolving odd-cycle Euler half-turn holonomy and the BCC step alphabet producing the signature-1/2 Ramanujan hypergeometric kernel.
theorems.boundary: No Ramanujan 1/pi functional is derived from holonomy alone.
